common_name: Vittata Fortunei Azalea (White Lilac-Striped Historic Azalea, syn. Vittatum)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; this historic clone is kept mainly by collectors and public gardens rather than general nurseries.

directions: Vittata Fortunei, also known as Vittatum, is an old Chinese clone of Rhododendron simsii that British plant collector Robert Fortune sent to England around 1850 after seeing it blooming near Shanghai. Its single flowers open white but are irregularly striped and flecked with lilac-purple, and individual blooms on the same plant can appear nearly solid white or solid lilac-purple rather than evenly patterned. USDA breeder Benjamin Yeo Morrison relied on it heavily as a seed parent at the Glenn Dale Plant Introduction Station, where it stands behind dozens of the released Glenn Dale hybrid azaleas. Grow it in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, and prune only right after flowering since next year's buds set soon afterward.
sources: Azalea Society of America — The Azalean
Journal of the American Rhododendron Society

common_name: Ho Oden Azalea (Lilac-Pink Purple-Spotted Hardy Breeding Parent)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; grown today mostly as a historic breeding clone rather than a common landscape plant.

directions: Ho Oden is an old hardy azalea clone, usually placed near the Kurume and Rhododendron mucronatum group, grown for lilac-pink flowers spotted with deep purple and edged in white on unusually narrow, strap-like petals. B.Y. Morrison valued it chiefly for the extra cold hardiness it carried from its mucronatum-type background, pairing it with 'Vittata Fortunei' to help produce the Glenn Dale hybrid 'Festive' and extend his breeding program's hardiness range farther north. The plant forms a dense, twiggy, compact evergreen mound typical of older Kurume-type azaleas. Grow in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, and prune immediately after bloom since next year's flower buds set soon afterward.
sources: Azalea Society of America — The Azalean
Journal of the American Rhododendron Society

common_name: Delos Azalea (Light Purplish-Pink Double Glenn Dale Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade.

directions: Delos is a double-flowered (hose-in-hose) Glenn Dale Hybrid azalea that B.Y. Morrison raised from a cross of 'Vittata Fortunei' and the Satsuki cultivar 'Warai Gishi', pairing a tender Chinese parent with hardier Japanese stock. Its light purplish-pink blooms carry an extra ring of petal-like stamens, giving a fuller, layered flower unusual among the mostly single-flowered Glenn Dale introductions. Morrison singled it out, along with its sibling 'Andros', as one of the few Glenn Dale doubles worth garden space even though double flowers were not his main breeding goal. Grow in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade, and prune only right after flowering since next year's buds form soon afterward.
sources: Azalea Society of America — The Azalean
Journal of the American Rhododendron Society

common_name: Kagetsu Satsuki Azalea (Flowery Moon, White-and-Pink Satsuki Parent of May Blaine)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Kagetsu, whose name translates as 'Flowery Moon,' is a dwarf Satsuki azalea cultivar prized for flowers so variable that almost no two blooms on the same plant look alike, ranging from faint blush pink to pure white with irregular penciling and shading between them. Its low, compact habit rarely exceeds a foot or so in height, placing it among the smaller traditional Satsuki selections long grown in Japan. B.Y. Morrison crossed it with the Satsuki cultivar 'Warai Gishi' to produce his Back Acres hybrid 'May Blaine' after retiring to Pass Christian, Mississippi. Grow in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, and prune only right after flowering, since this late-blooming type sets next year's buds soon after bloom ends.
sources: Journal of the American Rhododendron Society — Notes on Satsuki Azaleas and Their Allies
